title: Exploring Post-Hoc Disentanglement of Audio Foundation Models for Music Similarity
abstract: arXiv:2611.14415v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Audio foundation models like CLAP, MuQ, and MERT excel at capturing general musical similarity. On the other hand, their entangled latent spaces limit interpretability and fine-grained attribute control. Conditional Similarity Networks (CSN) address this by pairing a backbone representation model with learned masks that gate the embedding space into attribute-specific subspaces. However, existing methods train the backbone from scratch, rather than leveraging pretrained foundation models. We instead present a systematic study of post-hoc disentanglement, adapting CSN to gate frozen pretrained embeddings. We evaluate adding trainable parameters to adapt the embedding under different masking and pooling regimes across two datasets. translated_title: 探索音频基础模型的事后解耦以实现音乐相似度
translated_abstract: 诸如CLAP、MuQ和MERT等音频基础模型擅长捕捉一般性的音乐相似度。另一方面，它们纠缠的潜在空间限制了可解释性和细粒度的属性控制。条件相似度网络通过将骨干表示模型与学习到的掩码相结合来解决这一问题，这些掩码将嵌入空间门控为特定属性的子空间。然而，现有方法需要从零开始训练骨干网络，而不是利用预训练的基础模型。我们转而对事后解耦进行了系统性研究，将CSN调整为对冻结的预训练嵌入进行门控。我们在两个数据集上评估了在不同掩码和池化机制下添加可训练参数来适配嵌入的效果。我们的研究结果表明，最小程度的适配能力就足以使事后门控同时改善特定属性的解耦和整体检索性能，而池化、掩码和深度的选择……
tldr: 本文提出将条件相似度网络（CSN）应用于冻结的音频基础模型预训练嵌入进行事后解耦，证明仅需少量可训练参数即可同时提升属性特定的解耦能力和整体音乐检索性能。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically studies post-hoc disentanglement by adapting Conditional Similarity Networks to gate frozen pretrained audio foundation model embeddings, showing that minimal adaptation capacity is sufficient to improve both attribute-specific disentanglement and overall retrieval performance.
